primary_citation: Cal. Vehicle Code §11711 (Stats. 1959, Ch. 3 framework; treble damages + fees amendment ~1988)
short_title: Motor Vehicle Dealer Fraud — Civil Remedy with Treble Damages and Mandatory Fees
one_line_rule: A licensed California car dealer who commits fraud, misrepresentation, false promise, or deceit in a vehicle sale or lease is liable for actual damages, up to three times actual damages at the court's discretion, and mandatory attorneys' fees.

case_law.cite: Butler v. Sterling, Inc., 210 F.3d 371 (6th Cir. 2000)
case_law.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
case_law.key_rule: Yo-yo financing pattern documented: apparent finality of signed contract + delivery = representation that deal is complete; post-delivery demand for worse terms = evidence original representation was false; loss of trade-in as leverage = evidence of intentional misrepresentation.

case_law.cite: Lurch v. Ford Motor Credit Co., No. BC282636 (L.A. Super. Ct. 2003)
case_law.key_rule: California yo-yo financing damages methodology; conditional delivery 'complete deal' representation theory; Rees-Levering §2983.2 rescission right runs alongside §11711 damages; 'entire deal' doctrine — all components of the vehicle transaction package within §11711 scope.

violation_1_wrong_carfax.theory: Wrong CARFAX (different VIN) presented as vehicle history = direct misrepresentation in licensed dealer transaction
violation_1_wrong_carfax.damages: Reduction in fair market value from undisclosed prior damage/history
violation_1_wrong_carfax.evidence: Both VINs; CARFAX provided; actual VIN on vehicle

violation_2_yo_yo_financing.theory: Financing presented as complete at signing; post-delivery demand for return or higher rate = original financing representation was false
violation_2_yo_yo_financing.damages: Rate differential over loan life (if accepted) OR lost down payment + trade-in value (if vehicle returned)
violation_2_yo_yo_financing.evidence: Original contract terms; dealer's subsequent demand; $10,000 cash down payment lost

violation_3_title_defect.theory: Sale of stolen/stripped vehicle with title defect = per se misrepresentation about what was being sold; dealer knew or should have known
violation_3_title_defect.evidence: Theft/title investigation records; auction history; debt collection demand

combined_damages.treble: Up to ~$90,000+ at court's discretion; three violations support pattern finding
